# dbml-to-laravel (egyjs/dbml-to-laravel)

> Laravel package to generate and incrementally sync Eloquent models and database migration files directly from DBML (Database Markup Language / dbdiagram.io) schema files.

## When to Use

- Convert a DBML file or dbdiagram.io diagram into Laravel Eloquent models and migrations.
- Keep the Laravel schema in one declarative file and generate migrations from its changes instead of writing `make:migration` files by hand.
- Let AI coding agents change the database schema by editing one DBML file and running one command.

Not for: reverse-engineering an existing database into DBML, or generating controllers, factories or seeders.

## Overview

`egyjs/dbml-to-laravel` ([GitHub Repository](https://github.com/egyjs/dbml-to-laravel)) makes your DBML file (e.g., `database/schema.dbml`) the single source of truth for your Laravel database schema and Eloquent model boilerplate. It uses a pre-bundled Node.js DBML parser (`bin/parse-dbml.runtime.cjs`) and supports both initial full generation (`dbml:generate`) and incremental schema synchronization (`dbml:sync`) via safe `@dbml-sync` model markers.

## Requirements & Installation

- Laravel 8.x+
- PHP 8.2+
- Node.js 18+ runtime (parser is pre-bundled; `npm install` is not required in consumer projects)

Install via Composer:
```bash
composer require egyjs/dbml-to-laravel --dev
```

Optionally publish customizable model and migration stubs to `stubs/dbml-to-laravel/`:
```bash
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=dbml-to-laravel-stubs
```

## Core Artisan Commands

### 1. Initial Generation (`dbml:generate`)
Generates Eloquent models (`app/Models/*.php`), create-table migrations (`database/migrations/*.php`), and the `.dbml-sync.json` schema snapshot (written next to the DBML file, e.g. `database/.dbml-sync.json` — commit it):
```bash
php artisan dbml:generate database/schema.dbml
```
(Legacy alias: `php artisan generate:dbml database/schema.dbml`)

### 2. Incremental Sync (`dbml:sync`)
Compares `database/schema.dbml` against `.dbml-sync.json`, generates alter/create/drop migrations for schema deltas (columns, indexes, foreign keys, tables), updates `.dbml-sync.json`, and patches existing Eloquent models only inside `@dbml-sync` marker blocks:
```bash
php artisan dbml:sync database/schema.dbml --force
```
- Always pass `--force` when running in non-interactive shells or AI coding agents. Without it, `dbml:sync` exits `1` with a "re-run with --force" message when a confirmation is needed.

### Agent-friendly options (both commands)
- `--dry-run`: list files that would be written; writes nothing (no models, migrations or snapshot).
- `--json`: print a single JSON report `{"success", "dry_run", "written", "skipped", "errors"}` instead of console text.
- Exit code `0` = success, `1` = any error (missing file, parse error, reserved table name, unconfirmed prompt).

## AI Agent & Developer Conventions

1. **DBML as Single Source of Truth**: Modify `database/schema.dbml` and run `php artisan dbml:sync database/schema.dbml --force` instead of creating manual migrations with `php artisan make:migration`.
2. **Preserve `@dbml-sync` Model Markers**: Generated Eloquent models contain marker comments that `dbml:sync` uses for incremental patching:
   - `// @dbml-sync:table-property` ... `// @enddbml-sync:table-property`
   - `// @dbml-sync:fillable` ... `// @enddbml-sync:fillable`
   - `// @dbml-sync:casts` ... `// @enddbml-sync:casts`
   - `// @dbml-sync:relations` ... `// @enddbml-sync:relations`
   Never remove these markers, and write custom methods, scopes, or accessors outside the marker blocks so `dbml:sync` preserves them.

## Example DBML Schema (`database/schema.dbml`)

```dbml
Table users {
  id int [pk, increment]
  name varchar
  email varchar [unique]
  password varchar
  created_at datetime
  updated_at datetime
}

Table posts {
  id int [pk, increment]
  user_id int [ref: > users.id]
  title varchar
  content text
  created_at datetime
  updated_at datetime
}
```

Declare each relationship once: inline `[ref: > users.id]` or a top-level `Ref:` line, never both (duplicates fail to parse).

## Limitations

- Only `>` / `<` refs generate foreign keys and `belongsTo` / `hasMany`. One-to-one (`-`) and many-to-many (`<>`) refs are ignored (no `hasOne`, pivot tables or `belongsToMany`).
- `$hidden`, factories and seeders are not generated.
- Columns without `not null` are generated as `->nullable()`.
